descriptions.text: Enchanted Tiara of Mana Genita. A crystal tiara fit for royalty. Made in honor of all the lost children of the world. Because nothing helps sooth the tears of grieving parents like watching someone else dress up all fancy. +3 Intelligence Increased ability to detect mobs on the map. Removes automatic hostility by worshippers of Mana Genita.

beats.headline: White instead of purple
beats.text: Donut's boxes are mostly random scrolls and useless items to sell, but one of them, Carl is not sure which, holds a new tiara, and it poofs onto her head. It looks like her last one, with white jewels instead of purple. It is not as good as the one she lost: three intelligence, a better eye for mobs on the map, and no automatic hostility from the worshippers of Mana Genita. Who is Mana Genita, Carl asks. A goddess, says Mordecai, a pretty obscure one he does not think he has ever run across, big on spells, he thinks. There are thousands of them, and only a few are dungeon regulars.

beats.headline: Kept for a rainy day
beats.text: Since the crown, the white Tiara of Mana Genita is what Donut usually wears. But a Flawless Jeweler's Gem from a legendary box needs a setting, a yellow-orange citrine she insists will clash. They keep the old tiara, which might be useful one day, and buy a blank one from the gnome jeweler at the Desperado Club; it takes Donut twenty minutes, and a threat to leave, to choose a simple silver one. They pay 25,000 gold to have the citrine installed, and her dislike of the colour ends with the description: the Enchanted Tiara of the Inebriated Dragonfly.
